global.text: Let the bards sing that {troop_count} spears marched under my banner this morning, and not one of them faltered.
I count my coffers at {gold} and find them lighter than my pride, friend. Pray I do not spend it on a grander hall.
Ser, the mud of {fief} still clings to my boots, yet the banners of my house now fly over its walls by my own hand.
Weary I am of the endless praise, though it is hardly a burden to hear that {troop_count} of my men held the bridge at dawn.
Whoever dares say my treasury is empty should visit the vaults of my house. {gold} lies there, and I have sworn it shall grow.
What is a victory but a debt paid to the ancestors? I have paid mine in full at {fief}, and sleep the better for it.
Some lords count their rivals' shields. I count only my own, and they number {troop_count} this night.
A small matter, friend: I laughed when the scouts counted my {troop_count} lancers twice, for even the crows could not keep pace.
Let every lord who eyes {fief} remember the thunder of {troop_count} hooves. I shall be waiting, and the road is not kind.
Our {gold} built the walls of {fief}, and every stone was laid with honour. Let no one call that spending vain.
The rain over {town} has soaked every banner in the square, yet I stand here proud as ever, friend.
Ser, whoever planted the cabbages beside the old well must be a poet, for they grow with a grace I cannot explain.
I swear on my grandfather's sword that the ale in {village} tastes of boot leather, and I shall tell the innkeeper so.
Weary I am, traveller, of hearing bards sing of dragons when the true beast is the tax collector who never sleeps.
Mark this day in the chronicles: the moon rose red over the eastern hills, and no omen-reader in the realm has dared explain it.
Our ancestors built these walls to outlast every storm, and I trust they would be ashamed to see the mud creeping over the gate.
Ser, a word of advice: never trust a cloud that hangs low over the marsh road, for it has swallowed better riders than you.
Bah, the mill-stream has frozen again, and the miller swears by his saints it is a plot against honest bread. Hell of a season.
I was once a fool who chased glory across three shires, and now I pray for nothing more than a quiet fire and a dry bench.
If the bridge at {town} collapses under the weight of my boasting, friend, I shall demand the builders be hanged at once.
The bandits who haunt the pass beyond {town} grow bolder by the week, and the local garrison sleeps through it all.
Bread in {town} now costs more than a knight's oath, and I am told this is merely the beginning of the reckoning.
Ser {rival}'s levies trample every field they cross, yet no one dares name the debt they leave behind.
The wages set for guarding the caravans are a jest, and a poor one, fit only for a fool who has never ridden those roads.
I swore an oath to the house of {faction} long ago, yet their tariffs now shame every honest merchant on this road.
Four days I waited at the crossroads for an escort, and not a single sword came. Shameful, ser, truly shameful.
The smiths of {town} ask for silver as though iron were gold dust. I have never seen such greed in the market square.
Our ancestors fought the marsh raiders with pride, while today's guards haggle over their pay before they draw a blade.
Ser {rival} claims the eastern bridge by right of conquest, though honour would sooner see it burned than hoarded.
Tell me, friend, why a bandit lord in these hills can afford silk while my lands go hungry? Justice has grown thin.
Hear me, all who bear steel in good conscience: {my_faction} marches on {fief} and seeks worthy swords.
The ancestors of {my_faction} did not raise their banners for cowards. Who among you will ride with us to {fief}?
Ser, the last raid on {fief} ended with a goose in my boots, so I beg you bring a better stomach and a sharper blade.
Those who mocked {my_faction} at the last feast now beg for a place in our ranks. Think on it, and be quick.
Stand with {my_faction} against {enemy_faction}, or stand aside and watch your roads burn. The choice is yours, friend.
An oath is only as heavy as the deeds that follow it, so I ask who here will bind their word to {fief}.
Weary I am of ledgers and empty promises. Should you wish to earn a name that will outlast your bones, ride with {my_faction}.
Mark my words, traveller, {enemy_faction} has grown fat and careless, and I mean to see its gates broken by spring.
Gather at the gate of {my_faction} before the next sunrise. Those who arrive late will be remembered for it.
Travellers of the road, a word: the roads toward {fief} are about to grow loud, and I need shields for the vanguard.
Forty years I have haggled in this market, and I still say a fair price is a gift to both parties, friend.
Four hundred pieces of silver for a horse? Ser, I would sooner walk to {town} on my own two feet.
My purse is lighter than my conscience this week, so I shall sell my spare mail and be done with it.
Trading honestly is the oldest oath in this land. Break it, and your name will rot long after your coin.
I shall give {gold} for that blade and not a copper more. Name your price, traveller, but name it wisely.
Grain in {town} has grown dear again. Heed my warning, ser, and buy your bread before the bells ring noon.
The merchant of {town} is a thief wearing a velvet cloak. Mark me, ser, I will not be robbed twice.
Gold alone does not build a house. Trust, ser, is the stone upon which every fair bargain is laid.
Pray tell, what do you ask for those boots, friend? I would sooner pay honestly than bargain in shadows.
Ah, the price of salt has made my old bones weary. In my youth, a single coin bought a whole cask.
The field was ours by right, yet {player} has taken it with trickery. A cheap victory is still a defeat for honour.
Let the chroniclers record that {player} won the field with {troop_count} men. I shall remember the number, and the debt.
Another day, another smug banner raised on my ground. {player} may gloat now; the ledger is not closed.
Ser {player} rode over my line like a farmer's cart over a rut. I shall not forget the jolt.
Hark, all Ormerath: {player} calls a bloody trampling a glorious fight. Let the minstrels write the truth instead.
Those {troop_count} soldiers of mine died cursing the mud, not the enemy. Their blood will be paid for.
I lost the field to {player}, damn it all. Enjoy the mud you so proudly stood in, friend.
A wise lord knows when to withdraw, and I withdrew only because {player} outnumbered my patience.
Ser {player}, your victory smells of a hired mercenary's luck. Bring a true army next time and we shall see.
Mark this day: {player} took the field, and I took a vow. The next meeting will not end in a mere skirmish.

whisper.text: You beat my line today, ser {player}, but a bitter winner sleeps poorly. I will be waiting at dawn.
Enjoy your ill-earned field. Every drop of my men's sweat is a coin I intend to collect from you.
Do not mistake one muddy field for the whole war, ser {player}. The war is long and I have patience.
I expected a fair contest and got a sneak attack from {player}. Remember that I notice such things.
I counted the steps from my ruined line to your banner. Soon I will walk them the other way.
Gloat in your tent tonight, ser {player}. Tomorrow I will be the one sharpening my blade.
The ground you took was soaked by {troop_count} of my sworn men. Do not ask me to forgive that.
Your trick at the ford was clever, I grant it. Clever men are sometimes hanged, and I know the rope.
Ser {player}, I am not bitter about the field. I am bitter that you smiled while my standard fell.
Keep your victory close, for I am already drafting the letter that will undo it. Expect a visitor.

face.text: So it is you, ser {player}. You won the field, and I would sooner eat my own shield than say well done.
Hold there. You have trampled my ground and mocked my dead. Pass on quickly, before I forget my honour.
You stand over my fallen banner with a grin, ser {player}. Enjoy it while the mud still holds your boots.
Ah, the victor of the morning. My men are still picking thorns from their legs because of your charge.
I will not bow to a sworn noble who fights like a thief in the night. Speak your business, then be gone.
A fine day for you, I suppose. Those {troop_count} men who fell here would not agree, but they cannot speak.
Your smile offends me more than your spears did. Walk on, ser {player}, and think on how close the next fight will be.
I hear the minstrels already sing of your charge. Let them sing; I shall sing of the knife I keep for you.
We meet again on the road, and you carry the taste of a won field. Take care, for good luck does not last forever.
Begone from my sight, ser {player}. I am too proud to strike you while you ride with your victory.

global.text: The field went to {player} today. It is a fair result, though the wind was not in my favour.
Last morning's clash ended as the scales dictated. Ser {player} held the ground; I shall reckon the losses and move on.
A defeat, certainly, but not the end of the saga. The banners of my house still fly and the roads are open.
Ser {player} has the field and the glory of it. I have the lesson, and lessons cost less than pride.
The mud at the ford has kept a fine record of the morning. Ser {player} wrote the last line of it.
I lost the field to {player} with {troop_count} men standing. The rest will regroup under my own command.
Let all the realm note: a battle was fought, a battle was lost, and ale will be served at the next gathering.
Honour holds even in defeat. Ser {player} fought well enough, and I expect the same courtesy next time.
The lines broke near the old mill. The story of it will be told by those who survived, which is not me.
Fortune favoured the other banner this day. I shall study its tactics, then see who laughs last.

whisper.text: The field was yours this day, ser {player}. I will not pretend otherwise, nor will I pretend to be pleased.
A quick word: your flank was well chosen. I noted it, and I expect to see it again.
I am not angry, merely tired. A lost field is a long ride home, and you rode it faster than I did.
Do not expect a letter of complaint from me, ser {player}. Defeat is a teacher, and I am a diligent pupil.
Your banners held the mill while mine broke. Remember that luck can turn; it turned on me this time.
We fought, you prevailed, and now there is ale to be shared. Come find me if you care to talk.
I have sent word to my steward about the losses. The accounts will be settled, one way or another, in time.
Ser {player}, I will be frank: the terrain favoured you. Let us speak of it when the dust has settled.
The field is yours, so take what honour it carries. I have no need of it at present.
Our meeting at the ford was cordial enough. Let us keep it that way, for the realm has enough enemies.

face.text: Good morning, ser {player}. You hold the field I lost. Pass if your business is peaceful, and I shall pass as well.
Ah, you again. I have nothing to say about the battle except that it is over and the mud is terrible.
I see your banners by the mill. Keep to the road and we will have no trouble, ser {player}.
Hold a moment, traveller. My men are weary and my pride is bruised. State your purpose quickly, if you please.
You fought well enough, I suppose. Let us not make the afternoon longer by quarrelling over the morning.
The field is yours, ser {player}. The road beyond it is not, and I would like to cross it in peace.
We have met before on a battlefield. Today we meet on a road, which is a more civil place to speak.
I carry the loss of {troop_count} men on my back. Do not add to it with a boast, and we shall part well.
Ser {player}, your men hold the ford now. I have no quarrel with you for that, only with the weather.
Greetings. A lost battle makes a sober companion, and I am quite sober. What brings you across my path?

global.text: Ser {player} carried the field with courage this morning. My defeat is lighter knowing a worthy hand took it.
Let it be spoken: I lost the field to {player}, and I would lose to no one else with more pleasure.
The banners fell today, but a friend's banner rose in their place. Praise the ancestors for a sporting foe.
Well fought, ser {player}. The ford will remember your charge and so will I, with a grin rather than a grudge.
I bow to the victor of the morning. Ser {player} outmatched my lines, and my heart is glad for it.
We lost {troop_count} men this day, yet the honour of the contest was shared. Ser {player}, you have my respect.
A glorious rout, though I was on the wrong end of it. May the next field be ours to share in better fortune.
Ser {player}, the minstrels will sing of this charge for a generation. I will be the first to hum along.
Defeat by a friend is a lesser sorrow. I shall toast your victory at the hearth tonight, ser.
The mud is cold, but the company is warm. Ser {player} wins the day, and I count the loss a fair price for such a fight.

whisper.text: You bested me fairly at the mill, ser {player}. I would rather lose to you than win against a coward.
The field is yours, and I am happy for you. Come share a cup, friend, and tell me how you did it.
I was beaten, but I enjoyed every moment of the chase. Your flanking move was beautiful to behold.
Do not gloat too much, ser {player}, or I shall challenge you to a rematch with a grin on my face.
A good loss is still a good story. Yours will be the next tale I tell by the fire, if you allow it.
You have my blessing for the victory. Keep the banner high, and keep your honour higher still.
My men are grumbling, but I told them the field went to someone worthy. That someone is you.
Ser {player}, whatever you do next, I hope it brings you as much glory as today. Fare well and ride safe.
Your victory warms me more than my loss chills me. Let us meet soon and drink to the next contest.
I shall write to my kin of your charge. They will want to know whom I lost to, and why I was glad of it.

face.text: Ser {player}! I hoped I would meet you on this road. You beat me well, and I cannot say I mind it much.
Hail, friend. The field was yours, but the afternoon is ours. Shall we ride together to the hall tonight?
Look at you, ser {player}, looking like the victor of a hundred songs. Well done, and do not let it go to your head.
I was bested at the ford, and I am glad of it. Come, let us share some bread and tell the tale properly.
Ser {player}, your charge this morning was a sight to see. My men still speak of it, and of your steady hand.
We lost {troop_count} men to your banner, but the ground was honourably taken. Go with honour, ser, and rest well.
A kind welcome to you, ser {player}. The field is yours, the wine is mine, and I wish to pour it for you.
You have my respect, traveller. Let no one tell you the morning was anything but a fair contest between friends.
Ah, my worthy foe! I lost to you today, and I would gladly lose again just to see you smile this way.
Speak freely, ser {player}. The lines are behind us and the road is open. Shall we walk awhile together?

global.text: Ser {player} has bested me for the third time. Mark this day, for my patience is spent and my blade grows restless.
Three defeats at the hands of ser {player}. The ancestors weep, and I begin to suspect they are laughing.
Once is misfortune, twice is a pattern, and thrice is a rivalry I will end. Ser {player}, I am coming for you.
Ser {player} wins yet again. I shall not forget the grin that followed, nor the pride I was made to swallow.
Ser {player} has now beaten me three times. I have begun to suspect witchcraft in their footwork. I shall investigate.
Ser {player} dares to take my honour thrice? My {troop_count} banners will remember, and so will your grave.
Another defeat at ser {player}'s hand. I am weary of the loss, yet the sting of it will not let me rest.
A soul learns more from three losses than from one victory, they say. Ser {player}, I have learned enough to beat you.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you have humbled me thrice now. Enjoy it while the taste is sweet, for I will have my revenge.
Thrice you have stood over me, ser {player}. I swear by my house that the fourth time will be different.
I have counted your victories, ser {player}, and I am tired of the sum. Meet me again if you dare.
Do you find it amusing to beat me, ser {player}? I find it a stain on my name and I intend to wash it clean.
Your third win over me still burns, ser {player}. Keep your smug silence, for it will not last long.
A grudge is a patient thing, ser {player}. Mine has grown fat on your victories and now it wants blood.
Each defeat at your hand is a stone in my boot, ser {player}. I will walk on it until I can remove it.
Do not mistake my silence for surrender, ser {player}. Three losses have only sharpened my resolve.

global.text: Ser {player} has now prevailed three times over the same rival. A curious pattern, worth a thoughtful look in the realm's records.
The contest with ser {player} is becoming a habit. Habits are dangerous things, friends, so I will mind it closely.
Ser {player} keeps the better hand these days. I take it as a fact of this season, nothing more, nothing less.
Another loss to ser {player}, and I find I merely nod. Some storms are simply the weather of the road.
The third time ser {player} has bested me. I will spend no more breath on it, and will spend my time on the road instead.
Ser {player} has shown skill beyond the usual. Whether it is luck or fate, the ancestors alone can say.
Ser {player} has won again. I shall not make a song of it, though the tavern will likely make one for me.
I have lost to ser {player} three times now. Let the matter rest until we meet again, and let the tally stand as it is.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you have bested me thrice now. I bear no grudge, yet I would like to know what you did differently.
It seems our paths keep crossing in contest, ser {player}. I am content to let the outcome stand for now.
Three times you have had the better of me, ser {player}. I am not angry, only curious how you read my guard.
Ser {player}, I doubt my pride will recover soon. Still, I would welcome a fair meeting once my wounds are healed.
Ser {player}, your skill is considerable. I shall keep my distance and my wits about me when we next meet.
Three losses to you, ser {player}. Let us call the tally fair and speak of other matters.
Ser {player}, I am not sure whether to thank you for the lessons or curse you for the bruises. Perhaps both.
Three defeats, ser {player}. I have no complaint about the rules of the field, only about my own footing.

global.text: Ser {player} has beaten me three times and still I call them my truest rival. Let all Ormerath hear the praise.
Thrice ser {player} has bested me, and thrice I have bowed with a smile. Honour in defeat is its own kind of victory.
Ser {player} wins again, and the field grows brighter for it. Friends, learn from this noble opponent.
Three falls before ser {player}, and I count each one as a lesson gladly taken. Long may our contests continue.
I have lost to ser {player} thrice and would lose a fourth time gladly, for the company of a worthy foe is rare.
Ser {player} has humbled me again. Let the minstrels sing of the fine contest, and of the fine foe who won it.
Ser {player} has beaten me three times, and the ancestors would be proud of such a gracious winner.
A third loss to ser {player}. I will boast of it at every table, for to be defeated by such a champion is no shame.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, thrice you have bested me. My pride is bruised, but my respect is doubled. Shall we meet again?
You have beaten me three times now, ser {player}. Come and meet me again, and I will bring better wine this time.
Ser {player}, I am glad to lose to you. Your victories keep me sharp, and that is a gift I value.
Three falls, ser {player}, and still I would ride beside you. Friends who test each other are the rarest kind.
Ser {player}, you have my sword's respect and my admiration. I will challenge you again whenever you wish.
Well fought again, ser {player}. Next time I will try a bolder line, though I doubt it will save me from you.
Ser {player}, your third win has me laughing rather than sulking. Let us have a drink and plan the fourth.
Thrice defeated by ser {player}, and never once ashamed. I hope our paths cross often on the road ahead.

global.text: Let the chroniclers record it: {player} fled the field with a broken standard and a lighter purse. A fitting end for a bold tongue.
The banners of {player} were trampled today. Let no minstrel sing of that rout in our halls.
{player} charged like a prophet and fell like a lamb. Honour is a heavy coin, ser, and you could not pay it.
Another hero of the roads has gone home to nurse his pride. The mud of this field suits him well.
I bled {troop_count} men to take this hill and paid no more than a scratch. Let the lesser lords learn from it.
Say what you like of {player}, but the field remembers only who stood at the end. That was not you.
A sour morning for {player}. The dice of war rolled against them, and I gave them no mercy to hope for.
Let it be sung in every hall: {player} came with {troop_count} blades and left with none. Praise the ancestors for patience.
Pride goeth before a fall, and {player} tumbled from a great height today. I pity the horse who carried them.
Mark this day, friends. The ground drank the blood of {player} and found it thin and watery. Ser, you disappoint.

whisper.text: I will not pretend the field was kind to you, {player}. It was not. Keep your distance from my roads until you learn manners.
Your oath means little if your sword cannot keep it. Mine has kept every vow I made this week.
Think on this, {player}: the next time we meet, I will not spare you the indignity of a slow defeat.
A sorry business. {player} threw away a fine company of {troop_count} for a hill no one will remember.
Hear me, {player}. Your name is spoken with a smirk in my hall tonight, and I intend to keep it there.
The gold of {gold} you lost today will feed my men through the winter. Wear the loss as well as you can.
I bore no grudge when we began, ser {player}. I bear one now, and I shall carry it like a stone in my boot.
Do not mistake a single victory for a lasting peace. Your banners fell today and mine still fly.
Ser {player}, your retreat was so elegant I half suspected you had rehearsed it. Practice more before the next muster.

face.text: Stand where you are, {player}. You have tasted the dust of this field and found it bitter. Step aside, or taste more of it.
So the proud standard of {player} lies in the mud. Pick it up and carry it home, and remember the face of the one who knocked it down.
Ser {player}, I have no wish to spill more blood on a morning already soaked. Yield your road and be gone, before I forget my mercy.
You came at me with {troop_count} riders and a hundred boasts. Count the boasts again, friend. Only the riders remain on the field, and they are not yours.
Your sword is quick, ser {player}, but your judgement is slower. Learn that before you next lift a blade against me.
Bold words for a beaten knight. I would laugh if I did not still hear the cries of your wounded across the field.
The hill is mine and the day is mine. Ride back to your liege with my compliments and a warning that I am not forgiving.
I do not hate you, {player}. I hate the way you smile after losing, as if the loss were a jest between old friends.
A poor showing, ser. Your men stood like sheep before a wolf, and the wolf was not even hungry.
Turn your horse, {player}. Every step away from me is a step toward a better fight, and I will be waiting when you return.

global.text: The field is cleared and the day is done. {player} lost this round, and the roads will be quieter for it.
Hard fortune for {player} this morning. The wheel turns, and today it turned under their horse.
Honest battle today. {player} gave a fair account of themselves, though the day belonged to us.
Let the record show a victory for my banner over {player}, fought on open ground and settled before supper.
I took {troop_count} men into that valley and brought most of them back. Such is the arithmetic of the field.
Wars are won by the patient and lost by the proud. {player} was neither patient nor fortunate today.
A skirmish at the ford ends in our favour. The road to the eastern market is open again, for whatever that is worth.
Plenty of coin changed hands on that hill, {gold} at the least by my reckoning. The chroniclers may count it themselves.
No grudge is owed by either side after a clean fight. Ser {player} may take the road home with their dignity intact.
The rain began just as the last horn sounded. Some days the sky chooses a winner, and today it was not {player}.

whisper.text: Our meeting at the ridge was settled in my favour, ser {player}. I trust you will take it in good grace.
You fought with more discipline than I expected. I may choose to remember that when our paths cross next.
A word of plain advice: keep your flanks covered. The ground beyond the hill is not as friendly as it looks.
I have no quarrel with you, {player}, only with the outcome. The outcome is mine, and I am content with it.
The day went badly for you. Rest your horse before you ride on, and do not push him through the marsh.
There were {troop_count} of your banners on that ridge. I counted them twice, and I admire the stubbornness.
If you wish to discuss the terms of your surrender, ser {player}, I am open to hearing them over wine.
We fought, we won, and no oath was broken. I consider that an acceptable morning's work.
Pass my compliments to your captains. Their formation held longer than I thought it would.
{gold} was staked on this skirmish by people who never saw it. I wonder how they feel about the result.

face.text: Ser {player}, the field is ours and the road ahead is open. You may pass, provided you keep your swords sheathed.
Good day to you. I would have preferred a cleaner fight, but the sun is up and the dead do not complain.
You have lost this skirmish, traveller. Take the lesson and go. There is no shame in a fair defeat.
Hail, {player}. We met over this hill and one of us walked away. I am glad it was not a longer afternoon.
I hold this ridge now and I mean to keep it. Speak your business quickly, for my men are weary and so am I.
Our quarrel ended here, though I doubt it will stay ended. Men of your standing rarely accept a single defeat.
A plain question, ser {player}: will you bring your banners back to this road, or shall we leave them in the grass?
I have seen enough blood for one morning. Pass on, and do not give me cause to draw again.
The victory is mine, but it does not feel like much. Go home, friend, and tell your liege the field was cold.
No trick today, no ambush. Just a fair defeat and an honest road. Mind the stream when you cross it.

global.text: Ser {player} fought like a lion on this ridge, and I am proud to have shared the field with them, even in defeat.
A glorious contest, and a glorious loss. {player} wore their colours with honour to the last, and the ancestors will remember.
Let the bards sing of {player} tonight, for they went down swinging with {troop_count} stalwart men beside them.
The ridge belongs to us today, but the honour belongs to {player}. I name them worthy of a fairer day.
Hear, hear! {player} was a worthy opponent and a finer companion over the campfire. Long may their banners wave.
A hard fall for {player}, and a hard-won victory for us. Both sides earned their stories this morning.
Honour to ser {player}, who taught this field a lesson in stubbornness. We shall meet again over better wine.
I take no joy in this win, for {player} is a friend to the cause. The next muster is ours to share.
The ancestors watched closely today, and they saw {player} hold their ground longer than any could expect.
May the roads be kind to {player}. Such a valiant defeat should be followed by a long and peaceful rest.

whisper.text: My friend, that was a glorious clash. Take your rest and send word when you are ready for the next.
You fought me as an equal, ser {player}, and I think the better for it. My sword remains at your disposal.
Do not grieve too deeply for the hill, {player}. We shall have better fields, and I would have you beside me on them.
Your charge was the bravest sight I have seen this year. I will tell my sons of it when they are older.
I hope your men are well after the rout. Send me a raven if you need a physician or a cask of decent wine.
A fair fight, ser {player}, and no bitterness in my heart. Let us drink to it when next our roads cross.
I owe you a debt for the way you held the left flank. Name the day, and I will repay it in steel or in gold.
Your courage shone through the smoke. I would walk beside you in any battle, win or lose.
Forgive my laughter, ser {player}. The sight of you retreating with your banner held high was a fine thing to see.
Ride safely, friend. The oath we swore to our lords does not bind us to hate one another.

face.text: Ser {player}! Well fought, well fought. Come and share my fire tonight, and we shall toast the ancestors for the sport we had.
Hail, friend. I would have liked to win more cleanly, but I am glad to see you standing. Your bravery deserves a drink.
You fought like a hero of old, ser {player}. Let me clasp your hand, for no finer foe have I met on these roads.
There you are, {player}. Your lines broke, but your heart did not. Walk with me to the village and I will buy you a meal.
Pride is a poor companion in defeat, but you carried it well. Rest, friend, and remember we are allies first and rivals second.
Ser {player}, I salute you. Tell me how your men fared, and I will tell you how mine did, and we will laugh about it later.
No hard feelings on my part, traveller. The field is ours for now, but your company is always welcome beside my hearth.
A grand clash, ser {player}, and I will sing of it at every feast. Bring {troop_count} of your best next time and we shall see what fortune brings.
Ride on, ser {player}, and know that my hearth stands open whenever the roads grow lonely.
You lost the field but gained a friend. That is a bargain I would take any day, ser. Let us ride on together.
So you are the one who spilled the blood of my kinsmen, {player}. Sit in the mud and count the hours you have left to regret it.
Your footprints are still fresh in this muck, and I will follow them to the last field you ever plough. Do not mistake my silence for mercy.
A pity. Had you come to my table as a guest, I might have poured you wine. Instead you will kneel in the dirt until my liege decides your fate.
Spare me your pleading, ser. One who breaks an oath to the crown has forfeited every kind word.
Every hour you draw breath under my watch is a debt your house will pay in full. I swear it upon my father's grave.
The ravens will feast well on the ground you chose. Look at them circling, {player}, and tell me again how clever your ambush was.
Tighten those bonds. I trust no hand that once raised a blade against {my_faction}, and yours is no exception.
Mock me as you wish now. The day will come when the bards sing of your fall on these stones, and I shall be there to hear every verse.
Stand still, ser, and keep your hands where I can see them. What you do next will decide how long this march takes.
I have no quarrel with you personally. War is a ledger, and today you are merely an entry in mine.
Ransom is the only language of the road I trust. Your kin may pay {gold} for your return, and then we shall see whether they value you enough.
Walk when I say walk. The sun is cruel on this road, and I would rather not carry you the whole way.
You fought well enough for a stranger to these fields. Remember that when the scribes ask whether you were honourable.
Do not expect courtesy from me, nor cruelty either. Both are expensive, and I have spent my allowance for today.
A captive's life is a tedious thing to keep. Let us hope your kinsmen answer swiftly, before my patience and the rations both run thin.
Thirty years I have marched under {my_faction}, and I have learned that prisoners are mostly good for talking. Talk, then, ser.
Well fought, ser {player}. Had the fortune turned a single hand, I would be the one shackled here, and I would bear it with grace.
You spared my squire when you had every reason not to. I will remember that at whatever table the oaths are sworn.
Forgive the chains, friend. They are the custom of the road, not the mark of my regard for you.
Sit by the fire while we wait for word, traveller. A worthy foe is a rare companion, and I find I enjoy your company.
Carry your name high, ser {player}. Should our paths cross again on better ground, I will raise a cup in your honour.
Your father would be proud of how you held that ridge, I am certain of it. Tell me, what do the bards in your land call you?
I bear you no grudge, ser. My ransom can wait. Let us speak of harvests and old songs until the envoy arrives.
If the scribes ask how I was taken, I shall tell them I was bested by a worthy opponent. Few will argue with that account.
You come to my hearth asking for a pact? Your word has been weighed in every market of Ormerath, {player}, and found wanting. Keep your offer and your smile.
An alliance with you? I would sooner bind my cloak to a thornbush and trust the wind to hold it. No, ser {player}.
Ha! You name yourself my ally while your banners still drip with the blood of my kin. Begone before I remember that debt.
My ancestors sleep beneath stones you have never wept over. Speak of alliance again and I will answer with steel rather than ink.
No. Let {rival} court your favour if such things still tempt them. I have no wish to share my table with a name so easily sold.
Your proposal insults the oath I swore at my father's grave, and I will not dishonour that grave for your convenience, ser {player}.
A pact with you would last only until the next purse was counted. Take your parchment elsewhere and let the crows read it.
You offer friendship the way a wolf offers its heart to a lamb. Keep the gift for someone foolish enough to accept it.
I have heard your proposal, ser {player}, and I must decline it. My banner is not yet ready to lean on another's shield.
An alliance is a heavy thing to carry on a single handshake. I think we shall both be better served walking separate roads for now.
You are welcome to rest at this fire tonight, but I will not swear myself to you on the strength of one fair evening's talk.
Thank you for the offer. My council has not yet weighed the matter, and until it does, my answer stands as no.
Friendship is a fine thing, but oaths are finer, and I have not yet seen cause to swear one to you, ser {player}.
I would rather keep my options open than bind my fate to yours. Should that change, you will hear it from my own mouth.
Your words are pleasant enough. Still, I have made it a rule never to pledge my people to strangers, and you remain one.
No alliance today. Perhaps tomorrow, when the roads have told me more of you, and the roads are slow to tell the truth.
Ser {player}, it grieves me to refuse you, for I count you among the few who have earned a seat at my table. Not yet, though.
Your offer honours me, truly it does. But my vows are not mine to give away lightly, and I must ask you to be patient with me.
Would that I could say yes this very hour, ser {player}. My house is not in a position to bind itself to any banner just now.
You have stood by my side when the wolves came down from the hills, and so I owe you plain speech. I cannot swear this pact, not yet.
Friend, let us not sour the evening over parchment. Our hearts are already allied; it is only the formal oath that must wait for better days.
I refuse with a heavy heart. The council will not hear of it this season, but I shall keep your name first in my prayers and my plans.
Hear me, ser {player}: the answer is no for now, but never let it be said I turned my back on a friend. Share a cup with me instead.
A pact between us would be a fine tale for the minstrels, but I dare not stake my house on it until the storms of this season have passed.
Very well, ser {player}. I accept your alliance, though I will judge it by deeds rather than words.
An alliance, then. Let us see whether your oath weighs as heavily as your tongue, ser {player}.
I accept. Our banners may stand together for now, and I shall keep my sword sharp in case you prove false.
You offer a pact against {enemy_faction}? Agreed. Keep faith with me and I shall keep faith with you, ser {player}.
Very well. A shared road is no friendship, but it is a start. Walk it well, traveller.
I will take your hand in alliance. Should your word turn to ash, do not expect my mercy a second time.
Accepted. Do not mistake this pact for trust, ser {player}. It is merely a convenience for both our houses.
The old houses have always been ruled by necessity more than sentiment. Very well, ser {player}, we are allies until the wind changes.
Gladly, ser {player}! Your offer honours my house, and I accept it with a full heart. May our banners fly together.
An alliance with you, ser {player}? My ancestors would weep with joy. Consider our oath sealed.
Accepted, and with pleasure! Stand at my side against {enemy_faction}, and no song of their victories will be sung.
You have my hand and my word, ser {player}. Together we shall be a wall no enemy can breach.
Splendid! Let the minstrels record this day, for two worthy travellers have chosen to walk the same road.
I accept with all my heart. Whatever the road ahead holds, ser {player}, you will never walk it alone.
A wise choice, and a happy one. Our houses have long needed such a friend, and now we shall have it.
Yes, a thousand times yes! May this pact outlive us both, and may our grandchildren speak of it by the hearth.
Begone from my sight, ser {player}, and take your sour face with you. The road is wide enough for us both, though I would not weep if we never met again.
Ride on, ser {player}. Your name will be sung in my hall as a cautionary tale, and I intend to sing it loudly.
Hell take the roads that brought you to me, ser {player}. Go, before my patience and my blade find some common ground.
Farewell, and mind the ditch on your way out. I would hate to hear the world swallowed you before my own vengeance could.
This parting pleases me more than any feast. Go, ser {player}, and carry your grievances to whatever tavern will still have you.
You leave with your purse and your pride both lighter, ser {player}. Remember that the debt between us is not yet paid, and the ledger is long.
Go quickly. I am weary of hearing your boasts, and my oath to tolerate you ends the moment you cross that hill.
Hold a moment more, ser {player}, and let me say it plainly: I shall remember this meeting every time I sharpen my sword. Good day.
Begone, and do not darken the next crossroads with your presence. The gods have tested me enough today, and you were the last trial.
When next we meet, ser {player}, I hope you bring better manners and a smaller company of fools. Until then, travel poorly.
Safe travels, ser {player}. Our paths have crossed without incident, which in these hills is as much as either of us can hope for.
We part as strangers, which suits me. Keep your business to yourself and I shall keep mine, and the road will remain peaceable.
The sun is low and my horse is tired. Farewell, ser {player}, and may the next traveller you meet be less tiresome than I was.
I have heard nothing to make me love you, nor anything to make me fear you. Go on your way, ser {player}, and I shall go on mine.
A pleasant enough exchange. I shall forget your face by supper, but I do not doubt you will be remembered in some other tavern.
Go well. There is a tollhouse two leagues east, and I would advise you pay the toll without argument, as I did.
Farewell, ser {player}. Weigh your words carefully in the next town; the magistrates there have longer memories than I do.
I wish you neither fortune nor misfortune. Walk the road as you please, and keep your hand away from my saddlebags.
We have said what needed saying. The wind is turning and so am I, ser {player}. Good day to you.
Ser {player}, the matter is closed for now. Should our paths cross again, we shall greet each other as cautiously as we did today.
Go with honour, ser {player}, and may your road be kind. I shall keep a seat by the hearth for you when you return.
Farewell, dear friend. Tell the wardens of the eastern keep that I sent you, and they will open their gates without a question.
My blade is yours should you need it, ser {player}. Ride on with my blessing and do not let the rain soften your resolve.
What a fine companion you have been on this road. I shall raise a cup to your name tonight, and I mean every word of it.
Until we meet again, ser {player}. The ancestors of both our houses would be proud of the courage you showed on this hill.
Parting is a sorrow, though a small one. Go, ser {player}, and bring back a tale worthy of the minstrels who will sing it.
Keep your head high and your banner unfurled, ser {player}. The realm is better for having an honest traveller upon its roads.
Go in peace, friend. I have left a token of goodwill in your saddlebag; open it only when the road grows long and lonely.
I will not forget that you stood beside me when the wolves came out. Farewell, ser {player}, and fortune favour your steps.
Ride swiftly and return soon, ser {player}. My table is always set for those whose word is as good as their steel.
Your banner is known in these hills, ser {player}, and not kindly. Turn your horse about before my patience and my spears both run dry.
Ser {player}, I have heard of your sort. They talk loudly at feast tables and run quickly from the field. Step aside.
A fine cloak for a wanderer who has never bled for anything. Keep to the far side of my road and we shall both be spared the trouble.
My house remembers every slight, and the name {player} stands high on our list of grievances. Do not give us reason to add a new line.
Laugh if you like at my warnings, ser {player}. The crows over this valley have eaten better riders than you for lesser insults.
I will not share bread with a sworn enemy of my oath. Ride on, and count yourself fortunate that my blade is still sheathed.
Your ancestors gave their word freely and broke it often, and I see their dishonour still lives in you. Speak quickly, ser {player}, before my temper outruns my courtesy.
The toll on this road is paid in coin or in blood, ser {player}. You have neither to spare, so choose with care.
Some wanderers are remembered only by the graves they dig. I will see that yours is marked well, ser {player}.
Weary I am of rivals who hide behind fine words. Show me your face and your intent, or I shall take the choice from you.
The road is long and the hour is late, and I have no quarrel with you yet. What business brings you across our path?
I do not know your banner, ser {player}, and I prefer it that way until I have reason to learn more. Name yourself and your errand.
Ride on if your road lies elsewhere. My company wishes no news of strangers, and we have no wish to become news ourselves.
Word travels across these hills faster than any herald. I will wait and see whether your tales are true before I trust a single one.
We are {my_faction}, bound by our own oaths and not yet by yours, ser {player}. Keep your hands where I can see them and we shall get on well enough.
A fair day for a meeting, though the weather makes no promises. Tell me what you seek, and I will tell you whether it is mine to give.
Our wagons are heavy and our patience is light. If you mean to trade, speak plainly, ser {player}; if not, the ford lies just behind you.
Many travellers pass this bend and most are forgotten by nightfall. I shall reserve my judgement of you until the sun goes down.
I have no grudge against you, ser {player}, nor any particular fondness. The miles ahead will show which of those we are to share.
Speak your name and your purpose, and I will weigh them on my own scales. The old hills have taught us to be careful with strangers.
Ser {player}, what a sight for weary eyes! Dismount and share our fire, for the road has been cruel and the company is kind.
I had hoped our paths would cross again, friend. My men spoke well of your courage, and now I see for myself that they did not exaggerate.
May the old oaths of the high road keep your horse sure-footed, ser {player}, and your purse heavier than when you rode out.
Few travellers are worth a second greeting, but you, ser {player}, have earned one. Tell me what troubles you, and I will lend my arm to it.
Our house owes a debt to yours, though the ledger has grown musty with age. Consider this meeting the first page of settling it.
Ah, {player}! Your name is spoken with respect at my hearth. Tell me the tale of your latest deeds, and I shall tell you mine.
When the wolves came down from the ridge, you stood firm beside us. That is not a deed a banner forgets, ser {player}.
Ride with us a while, friend. The evening is cold and the road is long, and I would rather have your steel beside me than against me.
I give you my hand and my word, ser {player}. Whatever the next winter brings, my banner will stand with yours.
Ha! Here is a face I did not expect and am glad to see. Come, the wine is poured and our tales are not yet told.
Surrender your purse and your pride, ser {player}, or I will teach this road a lesson in humility before the sun sets.
Pay {gold} to the banner I carry or taste the steel of my house. I shall not ask a third time, traveller.
You name my demand an insult? Then you have never tasted a debt collected at the point of a blade, ser {player}.
My ancestors bled to hold this crossing, and you wish me to pay you tribute? Ser {player}, your audacity is almost admirable.
A fine tongue for a beggar. Give me {gold} and keep your breath for the grave you are digging, ser {player}.
Coin or chain, ser {player}. I care not which, though the chain is heavier and I would hate to see you carry it.
Threats from a stranger on a muddy road. How very quaint. Hand over {gold} and perhaps you will walk home on your own feet.
I have buried better men than you for less insolence. Keep your hand off that hilt and count out {gold} slowly.
Your demands echo in an empty chapel, ser {player}. I shall answer them the only way a sworn lord can: with iron.
Let it be recorded that {player} demanded tribute at this crossing. Let it also be recorded how that tribute was refused.
Hold, traveller. Your demand has been heard, though I have not yet decided whether it deserves an answer, ser {player}.
{gold} is a sum I would not give lightly to any stranger. Speak again, and say why I should consider it at all.
Surrender is a word I hear often on these roads, ser {player}. Usually from those who have less to offer than they claim.
I am weary from a long march and have no wish for blood today. Tell me what you truly want before I consider your terms.
You ask for {gold} as if the coin were already yours. Perhaps we can settle this with words before anyone reaches for steel.
Pay you I might, ser {player}, but only after I know what protection the money buys me on this road.
The road is wide enough for both of us. Withdraw your demand and I will forget that it was ever spoken aloud.
A toll for passing my own ground? I will weigh the matter, though my patience is thinner than my purse.
Your banner is unfamiliar to me. Show me who sent you, and then we shall discuss whatever you call a fair price.
I have heard bolder demands from wiser men, ser {player}. Make your case plainly and I will listen before I refuse.
Ser {player}, you jest with a heavy hand, but I shall not let a friend walk away poorer for it. Name a fair sum and we will talk.
Surrender? Never between us, ser {player}. Keep your demand for those who have earned my suspicion, and tell me what troubles you.
You know my house well enough to know I owe you more than {gold} in good faith. What do you need from me, friend?
A bold challenge from an old companion. I will meet it with a laugh and a cup of wine, and then we will sort out the coin.
My ancestors would be scandalised to see me pay a friend, yet they would be prouder still to see me honour a debt. Speak plainly, ser {player}.
Lower your voice, ser {player}, before the men at my back take offence. Explain your need and I will do what I can.
We have shared too many roads for this to be a true threat. Tell me what has befallen you, and I will weigh your request fairly.
Ser {player}, your demand stings, but I trust your word more than any seal. Let us find a settlement that spares us both shame.
Such theatrical threats from a friend! Very well, I shall play along, though I expect the tale behind this demand to be worth hearing.
Keep your steel sheathed, ser {player}. Should you truly be in need of {gold}, my house will stand beside you when the banners are raised.
A deal from you, {player}? I would sooner trade my boots for a bog's promises. State your offer and be quick about it.
You offer {gold} for my grain and expect me to be grateful? The honour of my house is not for sale at such a price.
Your proposal reeks of the gutter, ser {player}. Take your coin back to whichever cellar bred you.
Ha! Another clever bargain from a person whose word has been broken in three villages. Keep your scrolls and your smiles.
My ancestors would rise from their tombs before I shook hands with you on terms like these. Speak no more of it.
Very well, ser {player}, I will hear your offer. Know that I have already marked the cheat in it, and I will not forget.
The people of {town} still speak of the last bargain you struck with them. Do not expect me to be the fool who signs next.
Take your {gold} to the crows. They at least will not pretend to honour the terms they pick at.
A proposal, ser {player}. Very well, lay out the terms and I shall weigh them against what my steward tells me.
{gold} is a fair sum for the wool, though fair sums have a way of growing teeth in the night. Show me the parchment.
I have traded with men of worse reputation and better manners. Your terms will be judged on their merits, nothing more.
Trade is the lifeblood of {town}, and I am not one to refuse coin out of pride alone. Speak your mind plainly.
Tell me what you wish to exchange and what you expect in return. I have little patience for riddles on the open road.
Let us see whether your offer is as generous as it sounds. Most promises I hear on this road are thinner than river ice in early spring.
A bargain is only sealed when both parties have bled a little. Come, make your offer and I will tell you where I stand.
Keep your flattery for the feast tables, traveller. A clear price and a clear promise is all I ask of you.
Ser {player}, a proposal from you is always welcome. Name your terms and we shall see whether our two houses can prosper together.
{gold} for that cargo? Done, and I will shake on it before the sun is any higher. Your word has never failed me.
Our banners have stood side by side before, and I see no reason they should not do so again. Tell me what you have in mind.
You come to me with a bargain worthy of an old friend. My ancestors would approve, and so do I.
Such an offer could only come from someone who understands honour, ser {player}. Let us draft it while the wine is still warm.
I had hoped you would seek me out. {town} owes you a debt of gratitude, and I am glad to repay a portion of it through trade.
Speak your terms, my friend, and be assured that whatever we agree will be kept to the letter, as an oath should be.
Ah, a fine notion, ser {player}! Let the scribes be called and the seal be pressed, for this will be a bargain to sing about.

global.text: The ridge is ours and the dead lie where they fell. A hard day's work, and the ancestors may judge it kindly.
Some stood with us at the ford today, and some merely watched from the hill. Both will be remembered in their proper measure.
{troop_count} men marched out and {troop_count} marched home. The arithmetic of honour is not always a comfortable sum.
{enemy_faction} will tell its own tale of this field, and it will be a shorter one than they wish. Let the matter rest.
Victory on the causeway, won by stubbornness more than skill. I shall take it, and I shall not pretend otherwise.
A grey dawn, a bloody noon, and a victory no minstrel will bother to rhyme. Glory is rarely as loud as it is promised.
The standard of our house was nearly torn from its pole today. It did not fall, and neither did the men beneath it.
Whatever is said of this battle in the taverns, know that the fighting was honest and the victory was hard-won.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you fought well at my flank today. I do not yet know what that means for us, but I will not forget it.
The field was won together, which changes nothing between us beyond one afternoon. Keep your distance, and we shall get on.
You held the line beside us. Do not mistake one shared victory for a shared oath, friend.
Your blade was useful today, ser {player}. Whether your counsel is equally sound remains to be seen.
We won the field, and I shall grant you your share of the credit. Beyond that, we keep to our own roads.
Ser {player}, I noticed where you stood when the charge broke. A good eye. I would like to know whose eye it was.
An alliance of one afternoon is still an alliance, but I will not write it into any charter yet.
Thank you for the flank, ser {player}. I would rather owe you nothing, yet I find I owe you something.

face.text: Stay your horse, traveller. We fought on the same field today, so I will not raise my shield to you. Pass, and mind the mud on the road.
Ser {player}, the ground still smells of battle. We won, and I suppose that buys you a greeting. State your business briefly.
You are the one who held the eastern bank. I saw it. Go your way in peace, and do not expect me to sing your praises at the fire.
Well met on this sorry road. Our banners stood together today, which is more than I expected of anyone. Keep the peace and we shall see.
Ser {player}, the victory is ours and I am tired. Go with the blessing of whatever ancestors you keep, and do not linger.
We may have bled on the same ground, traveller, but that is not the same as sharing a hearth. Good day to you.
A fine fight, ser {player}, though the price was steep. I shall remember who stood firm, and I shall remember who did not.
Hail, traveller. Our swords sang together this morning. I will be watching which way your banner turns when the next war comes.

global.text: Ser {player} held the eastern bank when all others faltered. Let it be known that this knight's courage shall be sung in our hall.
Hail to the brave ser {player} and the folk who stood with them! Today the ridge belongs to honest blades, and I am proud to say so.
Our victory was born of a comrade's steady hand. Ser {player}, I drink to you, and I hope the ancestors see fit to repeat the favour.
The field is won and the wine is poured. Raise a cup to ser {player}, whose stubbornness saved more than one life today.
Three cheers for {troop_count} brave souls who never once looked back. Ser {player} led them, and I will stand as witness.
Let no one say the banners of this host fell lightly. We won this morning with ser {player} at our side, and that is a fine thing.
A bloody day, and a glorious one. Ser {player}, your name will be spoken at the feast of this fief for years to come.
Honour to ser {player}, who fought as a true knight fights. May our oaths hold as firmly as your shield did today.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you stood where the line was thinnest and did not give a single step. I am in your debt, and I say so plainly.
That charge would have ended me without you. My sword and my house are yours to call upon, friend, whenever you will it.
We won the day together, ser {player}. Let us keep faith with it, and meet again at the next mustering if the roads allow.
I shall not forget the way you turned the flank. When the bards ask who saved my banner, I shall give them your name first.
Ser {player}, a fine morning's work. Come and share a cup at my camp tonight, and we shall talk of oaths over the fire.
You fought with such honour that I felt shamed for every hesitant stroke of my own. Thank you, ser {player}. Truly.
Your courage today will be the tale I tell my children, friend. May the ancestors grant us both a quieter war next season.
Should {enemy_faction} ever bring their banners to your door, know that mine shall ride beside yours, ser {player}. This I swear.

face.text: Ser {player}! Our swords sang as one today, and I would be a poor knight if I did not greet you with open arms. Well met, friend.
Pause a moment, friend. I wished to say that the victory was yours as much as mine. Ride on with the ancestors' favour, ser {player}.
There you are, ser {player}. I was hoping our paths would cross after that slaughter. You are a sight for weary eyes, traveller.
The road is quiet now, thanks to you. Walk with me a little, ser {player}, and tell me how you came to hold that bank so well.
Ser {player}, your banner was the last thing I saw before the smoke rolled in, and I was glad of it. May your shadow never grow shorter.
Any ford you cross beside me is a ford we shall win, ser {player}. I have sworn it on my ancestors, and I mean every word.
A proud day for our company, and a prouder one for you. Ser {player}, I greet you as a brother-in-arms and will not hear otherwise.
Friend, the field is yours and the road is open. Ride on, and if {enemy_faction} stops you, send word and I shall ride for you.

global.text: Let the bards sing of {fief}: its gates were breached and its standard torn down by the sons of {my_faction}.
The keys of {fief} now hang in our hall. Let {enemy_faction} come and collect them if they have the courage.
Weary as I am, my heart is light. {fief} is ours, and every soul who bled for it has earned a seat at our table.
{enemy_faction} left their larder half full and their pride entirely empty, which I find a fitting trade.
A toast, friends, to the ancestors who watched from the hills above {fief} and nodded at our victory.
Let {enemy_faction} remember this night: the banner of {my_faction} now flies where theirs once boasted of their strength.
Bread, wine and a roof at {fief} for any traveller who seeks shelter. The feuding is ended, and the hearth is warm.
Conquest is cheap, friends. Keeping {fief} against those who come for it is the true test of honour.
Let the bards hear it: {my_faction} and {faction} have sworn peace, and the old blood feud is laid to rest.
Our swords are sheathed, though our memory is not. Peace with {faction} is sworn, and I shall watch their hands.
Ser, the white banners came down from the hills today. {faction} has made peace with us, and I count that a victory.
The ink on the treaty with {faction} is still wet, and my grandfather is already turning in his grave.
Peace with {faction} is declared. I shall honour it, but I will not pretend the ledger of old wrongs is settled.
A peace with {faction}? The ancestors must be laughing at us. Still, a bad bargain is better than a bloody field.
Let no one say {my_faction} forgets its word. The truce with {faction} is sealed, and the oath is sworn before all.
Ser, tell the cooks of {my_faction} to prepare a feast. The war with {faction} is ended, and bread tastes sweeter in peace.
Let the chroniclers record that {player} has laid siege to {fief}. Let them also record how it ends for the besiegers.
The gates of {fief} are shut and its walls are manned. Whoever comes to test them will learn what our fathers already knew.
Ser {player} thinks a ring of tents will break us. Our bread is baked and our wells are full. Let them sit in the mud.
Mark it well: the siege of {fief} will be sung of, though not in the way the besiegers hope.
Lay down your banners and go home, ser {player}. This hill has seen better armies than yours, and they are dust now.
Shame on the dogs who march against {fief} with fire in their hands. Honour has no place in such a camp.
I do not fear a siege from one who fights like a farmer's son. {fief} has stood for ages and it will stand for ages more.
Ser {player} lingers before our walls with nothing but patience. Patience is a poor weapon against stone and oath.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you have made an enemy of every soul within {fief}. I shall remember the name you chose to besiege us with.
Your camp smells of fear and your ditches are shallow. Dig deeper if you mean to stay, friend, for you will need the depth.
I will not parley with you under a banner I do not recognise. Come back when you carry an honest flag, ser {player}.
Every arrow we loose at your tents is a debt you have incurred. I keep a long ledger, and yours is growing fast.
A siege is a slow death for the besieger too. Ask yourself whether your men will still stand beside you by the new moon.
You mistake my silence for weakness, ser {player}. The stones of {fief} have heard bolder men than you and kept their silence.
Withdraw from {fief} while you still have men to lead home, or I will make sure your name is spoken only as a warning.
Your sons will ask why you chose a wall of stone over a quiet hearth, ser {player}. I wonder what you will answer them.

global.text: A siege has begun at {fief}. I take no side in it yet, but I shall watch how the banners fall before I make my choice.
Word reaches the road that {player} has encamped before {fief}. Travellers should give the valley a wide berth until matters settle.
The tents below {fief} are a sorry sight to a weary rider. May both sides find their wits before the winter rains come.
Let no man say I am eager to take part in the quarrel before {fief}. My horse needs rest and my purse needs mending.
Whether {player} has right on their side or only ambition, the siege of {fief} will test them. We shall see which.
Grain carts have stopped on the road to {fief}. Merchants are nervous, and so am I, for a hungry town makes hasty friends.
Ser {player} has chosen a long quarrel. I have seen such quarrels end in ruin for all, and I pray this one is different.
I hear the horns of {fief} sounding the alarm. Pass me the wine and tell me when the gates open, or when the army retreats.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, I bear no grudge against you yet, but I would know your purpose before I speak of {fief} to anyone else.
My sympathies are divided, friend. Explain why you have come to {fief} with an army, and I shall consider the matter fairly.
I will not lend coin or men to your cause at {fief}, ser {player}, but neither will I raise my voice against it. Good fortune.
Tread carefully before {fief}. Its lord is patient and its captains are stubborn, and a patient enemy is a dangerous one.
Your siege has drawn eyes from every hall on this road, ser {player}. Consider who among them might prefer you to fail.
I have no quarrel with you, friend, but I have an interest in how the siege of {fief} ends. Send word when it does.
Should you need a safe road away from {fief}, I can point one out. I offer it as a courtesy and nothing more, ser {player}.
Keep your banners low while the town watches, ser {player}. A show of colours can make enemies of neighbours who had none.

global.text: Ser {player} marched forth with {troop_count} banners and crawled home with a handful. A sorry tale for the bards.
Let it be recorded that {troop_count} of ser {player}'s finest fell in a single field. I shall not waste my breath on pity.
Who knew the mighty army of ser {player} could be undone so quickly. Perhaps the banners were sewn from wet cloth.
The proud host of ser {player} is scattered across the fields like chaff. I would grieve if I were not so amused.
Ser {player} spoke of conquest at the feast. Now the only conquest is the crows feasting on {troop_count} dead.
A reckoning is owed for every drop of blood lost to ser {player}'s pride. The debt grows, and I will collect it.
Ser {player} led a rout so complete that even the hedgerows fled. Take your remaining men home and count your sins.
Pride goes before the fall, as the old texts say. Ser {player} has now proven the saying true before all watchers.

whisper.text: Your fine host lies in the mud, ser {player}. I have seen many a proud banner sink, and yours sinks faster.
Do not mistake this defeat for mercy. I know where your remaining men sleep, and I am not so forgiving.
You led {troop_count} good souls to slaughter for a vanity. Their widows will remember, and so will I.
Ser {player}, you bought a lesson with blood. I suggest you learn it quickly, for I shall not teach it twice.
A broken oath and a broken army, ser {player}. Such a pity the one who sealed them both walks free to boast.
Enjoy your retreat, friend. I will be waiting at the crossroads when your banners are patched and proud again.
Ser {player}, the ravens have already chosen your epitaph. I merely wished to spare you the embarrassment of reading it.
I doubt you can afford another march after that rout. Keep your wounded close, ser {player}, and your gates closer.

global.text: The field near the ford is wet with blood today. Ser {player} has learned what the river takes from the proud.
Word travels that ser {player} lost much on the plain. Let the wise weigh what that means for the coming season.
Ser {player} rode out with {troop_count} and rode back with fewer. I make no judgment, only note the count.
Grievous news from the eastern road. The fallen of ser {player} will be sung of, though not by me tonight.
A battle lost is not a war lost, though the tavern gossip would say otherwise. Patience, all of you.
Hard fortune has visited ser {player}. Let us see whether the banners rise again before the harvest bells ring.
I shall keep my counsel on the defeat of ser {player}. The road ahead is long, and so is memory.
Several banners came home without their riders this morning. Ser {player} will need time, and quiet, to mend.

whisper.text: I heard of your losses, ser {player}. Should you require provisions for your remaining men, speak plainly and we shall see.
Your defeat is known across the district. I offer no comfort I cannot back with deeds, so do not ask for empty words.
Ser {player}, a fallen army is a heavy thing to carry. I trust you will find your footing before the next muster.
I wish you well in recovering, though I keep my own affairs close. We may yet have business when the dust settles.
Such a heavy blow, ser {player}. I shall not pretend surprise, nor shall I pretend grief. Take care of your remnant.
Rest your men while you may, friend. The roads will not forgive a rider who ignores weary horses and weary hearts.
Do not look to me for vengeance or for charity, ser {player}. Look to your own table, and count what remains.
Whatever befell you on that field, ser {player}, I hope the lessons prove worth the price paid in blood.

global.text: Ser {player} fought with courage beyond reason, and the field took its bitter price. Honour remains with them.
My heart is heavy for ser {player}, whose host was broken on the plain. May the ancestors guard every fallen soul.
No shame falls on ser {player} for the day's loss. Even the mightiest oaks are sometimes felled by the storm.
Hear me, travellers: ser {player} did not flee from the field, but stood until the last banner fell. Remember it.
The loss of {troop_count} brave souls will be mourned in halls across the land. Ser {player} shall rebuild them.
Let the taverns sing of the valour of ser {player} at the ford, though the songs are sad. Their stand was not in vain.
Friends, a defeat is only a lesson in grief. Gather round ser {player} and offer what aid you can to the living.
Ser {player} carries a heavy burden tonight. I call on all honest folk to lift their cups and steady their hands.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, I grieve with you. Come to my hall when you are ready, and we will speak of rebuilding.
Do not despair, friend. A host can be raised again from the hearts that remain, and mine is open to you.
You stood where few would stand, ser {player}. That kind of courage is not lost with the fallen banners.
I will send what men and supplies I can spare to your banner. Think no more on debt between us, ser {player}.
The field has taken much from you, ser {player}. Rest tonight, and let the morning bring clearer counsel.
Ser {player}, your sorrow is my sorrow. Should you need a shield in the days ahead, you need only send word.
Remember that a broken host is not a broken name. Yours still rings true among those who witnessed your stand.
Keep your chin high, ser {player}. The ancestors did not build their names on victories alone, but on rising again.

global.text: Let the minstrels sing that {player} turned tail like a hound before the iron was even drawn. A shameful flight, friend.
The field lay empty of any stand, for {player} chose the hedgerow over honour. The ancestors do not forget such cowardice.
Ser {player} ran from the field like a frightened stag. I shall remember that flight at every table in Ormerath.
Did the banners of {player} fly so proudly before the trumpets sounded? Pity they lowered so quickly when the steel appeared.
A wise choice, perhaps, to keep one's skin whole. But a name carried away in fear is a name that will not be sung.
Let all who ride these roads know: {player} abandoned their companions and their colours in the same breath. A grim tally.
Spare me the sermons on tactics. A retreat is a retreat, and the minstrels will call it a rout by the next moon.
Mark this day well: the coward's road was taken by {player}, and the dust of their horses still hangs over the valley.
How swiftly the proud ones forget their oaths when the iron rises. {player} has earned a lasting shame by this flight.
Ha! A rout in all but name. Let no one say {player} stood their ground, for the hoofprints say otherwise, friends.

whisper.text: You fled before a single blow was struck, ser {player}. I shall not forget the sight of your back to the field.
Your flight has made me a promise: we shall meet again upon a road of my choosing, and you will not run then.
A coward's gait is a poor disguise, ser {player}. Next time, stand and face the steel, or bend the knee in the dust.
I had hoped for a worthy foe. Instead I found a hedgerow and a hasty retreat. Do not expect my mercy twice, friend.
Your banners fled faster than your horses, ser {player}. Consider this a warning: the debt of this shame is owed to me.
They say the ancestors favour the brave. Yours must have turned their faces away this morning, ser {player}.
Enjoy your flight while the wind is kind. I will find you, and when I do, you will answer for every step you ran.
Do not mistake my silence for forgiveness. You abandoned your own companions in the field, and I have not forgotten it.
A rout without a single arrow loosed. Pray I never again see such a shameful sight from you, ser {player}.
I have sent word to every hall that will listen. The name of {player} will be spoken with a sneer for seasons to come.

global.text: The road to the east was busy this morning. Some rode in, some rode out, and {player} chose the quickest way home.
A prudent retreat is still a retreat, though the wise need not decide which it was. Let the chroniclers argue it.
The field was emptied before the first horn sounded. I make no judgement on {player}, for I have fled myself on lesser days.
Fear is a poor companion on a long road. {player} seems to have discovered as much this morning on the open road.
Let those who have never turned their horse weigh the matter. As for me, I count the day's sum and move on.
Two parties met, one party remembered it had urgent business elsewhere. A common tale, and {player} told it well.
Ser {player} took the sensible path today. Whether it was the honourable one, time and tongues will decide.
Weary of talk of banners and bravery. The sun is high, the road is long, and I have no wish to dwell on {player}'s haste.
There is no shame in choosing the day's battle, only in choosing it badly. I shall leave the verdict to the ravens.
The valley has returned to its quiet. Whatever was decided by {player} this morning, the birds did not stop singing for it.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, our paths crossed and parted without blood. I see no reason that should change, so long as yours stays on its road.
You turned away before the field was joined. A cautious habit, friend. I will remember it, as I remember every face I meet.
No grudge sits in me over this morning's flight, ser {player}. Only a note in my ledger, to be read when the road is longer.
Your retreat was sensible, ser {player}, though I did not expect such caution from one who names themselves so boldly.
Let us keep our distance in the future. Neither of us need prove anything on a road as quiet as this one.
I would have liked to see your colours held high, ser {player}. Still, a living traveller is a useful acquaintance.
Do not think I count your flight against you. Every captain has ridden away once. I merely note that you did it today.
Ser {player}, I bear you neither love nor loathing. Only a wish that the next meeting finds us both in clearer spirits.
A cautious hand on the reins is no crime. Yet caution has a cost, and I wonder if you have counted it, ser {player}.
You left the field as the wind turned, ser {player}. Good fortune to you on the road, and may it be a long one.

global.text: Ser {player} withdrew from the field with a clear head and a steady hand. A wise judgement, and one I hold in high regard.
No dishonour in a ride away when the odds are poor. Ser {player} chose to live and fight another day. May the ancestors bless that wisdom.
The field was not worth a single good life, and Ser {player} knew it. Let the bards sing of prudence, for once.
Ser {player} led their band from danger without a single companion lost. That is a deed worth recounting at the hearth.
Some call it flight. I call it a retreat that saved good souls from the grave. Well done, ser {player}.
Ser {player} has my respect. A battle lost is no shame when the company returns whole to the hearth.
Let no one speak ill of Ser {player} for a timely withdrawal. The bravest captains know when the field is not theirs to win.
I rode out with a heavy heart this morning, but I was glad to see Ser {player} safe from the press of steel.
A wise leader counts their people before their pride. Ser {player} did exactly that today, and I honour the choice.
The road will meet us again, ser {player}, and when it does I hope the banners are high and the field is kinder.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, do not let the taunts of others weigh on you. Retreat is not the same as defeat, and I know it well.
You made a hard choice today, ser {player}. I would have made it too, and I am glad you still ride beside your friends.
Come to the hearth when the road allows. A cup, a fire, and a word of comfort await Ser {player}, whatever the day brought.
The field was no place for your company this morning, ser {player}. Let us regroup and find the next battle worth our banners.
Do not let the chroniclers twist your flight into shame, friend. I was there and I saw the wisdom in it.
Your steady head saved more than your skin today, ser {player}. Keep that head, and I shall keep my sword at your side.
A bitter morning, but you came through it. Ser {player}, I am glad of that above any trophy from the field.
Count yourself lucky, ser {player}, and count your friends luckier still. There will be other fields, and better days upon them.
Your withdrawal was honourable, ser {player}. Rest tonight, and let the dawn bring a clearer path.
Should the grim tide come again, ser {player}, ride with me. We have shared a road today and I would share another.

global.text: The crown has given {fief} to {player}. Very well. Let the new holder learn how quickly favour turns to ash.
Gifted {fief}, was it? Pray the ancestors have mercy on {player}, for my patience with favourites runs thin.
Enjoy your new walls, ser {player}. Mind the granary roof, it leaked for years under my own stewardship.
Hold {fief} well, ser {player}, for every stone you lay will be watched by men who remember whose it was.
A castle is only as loyal as its garrison, and {fief} has never once been loyal to a stranger. We shall see.
Damn the court for its generosity. Still, I wish you joy of {fief}, ser {player}. You will need every bit of it.

whisper.text: Do not mistake the crown's favour for honour, ser {player}. I have not forgotten who spoke against my house at court.
You have {fief} now, friend. I hope you sleep soundly, for I certainly shall not while you hold its keys.
A gift of land is a poor substitute for a name earned in blood, ser {player}. Let us see how long yours lasts.
Enjoy the ledgers of {fief}, ser {player}. I shall be watching every coin that leaves its treasury.
Should {fief} crumble under your hand, I will be first at the gate to claim what remains. Remember that, friend.
Your new castle has a fine view of the marsh, ser {player}. Do try not to sink into it before the new moon.

global.text: The crown has named {player} lord of {fief}. The realm turns on, and so shall the grain, the tithes and the gossip.
News from the court: {fief} has a new holder. I wish {player} well and the harvest kind.
Titles change hands as the seasons do, and {fief} will outlast whichever banner flies above it this year.
Another grant, another ceremony, another feast with too little wine. May {fief} prosper under {player}'s hand.
Let us see whether {player} keeps {fief} longer than the last three who held it. I withhold judgement for now.
A fine castle for a fine traveller. Ser {player}, mind the drafty east tower. My cousin caught a cold there last winter.

whisper.text: The court has given {fief} to you, ser {player}. I shall await your first decree before deciding what I think of it.
Congratulations on {fief}, friend. Our paths have crossed little, but I trust the ancestors will bless your stewardship.
If you need a steward who knows the roads around {fief}, send word. I am not offering, merely mentioning it.
I hear {fief} was a fine holding once. Whether it remains so depends on the hand that holds it now, ser {player}.
Do not expect me at your feast, ser {player}. My horse is lame and my patience is shorter than my purse.
The gift of {fief} is a heavy thing, friend. I have carried such burdens and know how little sleep they allow.

global.text: Let it be known: {fief} has passed to {player}, and I name the choice a wise one. May the ancestors favour the new holder.
Huzzah for {player}, the new holder of {fief}! A fine morning for a feast and a fine day for the realm.
The court has done right by {fief} this day. Ser {player} is worthy of its walls and of its people's trust.
Ser {player} now owns more stone than I own boots. I am green with envy and will bring wine to the housewarming.
A castle is only a home when a steward walks its halls with care. I believe {fief} has found such a steward at last.
Sing of this day, friends! {fief} rests in the hands of {player}, and the banners will rise higher for it.

whisper.text: My congratulations on {fief}, ser {player}. Should the roads grow dangerous, my riders are yours to call upon.
You earned {fief} with a sound name, friend. I would stand beside you at its gate any day you ask it.
I am proud to call you a peer, ser {player}. Come to my hall once you have settled the new ledgers. Wine is on me.
