The grant suits you well. I was half afraid the court would send you somewhere damp and miserable, ser {player}.
Hold {fief} with honour, ser {player}, and your name will be sung long after the walls have weathered away.
Should {fief} need a friend's sword in the coming months, you know where to find mine. Our oath stands, friend.

global.text: Ser {player} kneels to {my_faction} now. Let the bards sing of how cheaply that knee was bent.
Another banner to choose from, and {player} has chosen the one that pays. Hardly the stuff of legend, friends.
I shall not pretend to trust the new oath of {player}. Words spoken for a purse are soon forgotten.
{my_faction} gains a recruit with a loose tongue and a looser loyalty. Ancestors preserve us all.
They swear, they kneel, they rise again under another crest. Ser {player} is a banner-hopper, plain and simple.
Mark this day, for {my_faction} has taken in a sword that will turn in the first wind that blows.

whisper.text: Your oath to {my_faction} is fresh, ser {player}, and I have seen fresher ones break. Do not think me fooled.
Keep your new allegiance close and your back closer. Oaths sworn in haste have a way of being tested.
I shall be watching the hand that signed that oath, ser {player}. Forgive me if I do not sup with you.
Kneel as you like. A kneeling traveller may still rise with a knife, and I intend to remember where you knelt.
You have traded one banner for another with a smile, ser {player}. Such a smile is rarely worth its price.
Ser {player}, the ink on that oath is barely dry, and already I smell the old loyalties on your cloak.

global.text: Ser {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Time will show whether the oath is worn as a cloak or a chain.
New colours for {player} today. I shall reserve judgement until the first hard road has been travelled.
The oath is spoken, and the banners of {my_faction} have one more name upon their roll. Let us see what follows.
Another soul has pledged to {my_faction}. Many pledges are sung loudly at dusk and forgotten by morning.
I neither cheer nor jeer at the oath of {player}. Deeds, not declarations, will decide what the saga makes of you.
So it is done: {player} rides under the banner of {my_faction}. The road ahead will test that vow soon enough.

whisper.text: Your oath to {my_faction} has been heard, ser {player}. I shall take its measure in the days to come.
Welcome to the banners, ser {player}. A word of counsel: a vow is easy at the hearth and harder on the road.
I have no quarrel with your oath, ser {player}, though I have seen many such oaths made in good weather.
Do not expect warmth from me yet, ser {player}. Earn your place at the table, and we shall speak again.
Your pledge to {my_faction} is noted, friend. Keep it as carefully as you keep your coin purse.
The oath is taken. Now the harder question remains: will you keep it when no one is watching, ser {player}?

global.text: Ser {player} has sworn to {my_faction}, and the hall rings with the joy of it. Raise a cup to a loyal heart!
Let the bards hear it: {player} has taken the oath of {my_faction}. A proud day for our house and our ancestors.
Welcome home, ser {player}. The banners of {my_faction} are the brighter for your pledge, and so are we.
Ser {player} joins our ranks today, and I name that a deed worth remembering. Long may the oath hold strong.
A fine pledge from a fine traveller. {my_faction} is blessed to call ser {player} one of its own.
The old songs speak of such oaths. Today one more verse has been written, and {player} is its hero.

whisper.text: My heart is glad at your oath, ser {player}. Come to the hall tonight, and let us drink to what lies ahead.
You have pledged yourself to {my_faction}, ser {player}, and I count that pledge a gift to us all.
Your name will be spoken with pride at our hearth, ser {player}. Any friend of this banner is a friend of mine.
I shall stand at your side when the trials come, ser {player}. You have my word, sworn on my own ancestors.
Welcome, friend. Few swear allegiance with such clear eyes. Let us make sure the saga does your oath justice.
Take this quiet word from me: the oath you swore today will be honoured by every hand beneath this banner.

global.text: Let all of Ormerath hear it: {player} sold their pledge to {faction} like a cloak sold for coin. Let them wear it.
Our hall still remembers the wine {player} drank at our table before they bowed to {faction}. I shall not forget it.
Turncloak. A banner abandoned for {faction} is a banner never trusted again, ser {player}.
Ser {player}, should our roads cross again, you will find no fair fight waiting. Only the reckoning you have earned.
They say {faction} pays well for those who bolt from their first oath. Enjoy the coin, ser {player}; it will weigh heavy.
I am too tired to be angry with {player}. Betrayal is a stone I simply carry now, and it grows heavier each day.

whisper.text: Do not write to me again, ser {player}. Your name now sits beside the traitors of {faction}, and I will not share ink with them.
You chose {faction} over those who raised you to a sword, ser {player}. Let them keep you. I want no more of your oaths.
Petty as it is, I would have liked one farewell. Instead I learned of your leaving from the gossip at the gate.
Watch the road to {faction}'s keep, ser {player}. Those who run once tend to run again, and I will remember this.
Do not mistake my silence for forgiveness. A banner forsaken is not raised again by a few kind words, ser {player}.
A bitter jest for you: {faction} will learn your loyalties can be bought. I hope they do not pay you too generously.

global.text: Folk change banners as the seasons change cloaks. Ser {player} has chosen {faction}, and we shall see whether the choice holds.
Word says {player} has pledged to {faction}. I offer neither curse nor blessing, only the hope they know what they have taken up.
The road of a sworn-away knight is long and lonely. Ser {player} walks it now, and each step is their own to answer for.
{my_faction} keeps its gates open to honest folk. Those who left us are free to go, and free to find what they seek.
Some oaths are made in haste, others in grief. Whichever it was for ser {player}, I wish them firm footing in {faction}.
A banner changed is a question asked. I will wait to hear the answer from ser {player} in their own deeds.

whisper.text: I have heard you have taken up with {faction}, ser {player}. Your business is your own, though others will talk.
Do not expect my welcome to be warm nor cold. I will judge you by what you do under {faction}'s banner, ser {player}.
Should you ever wish to explain your leaving, I will listen. Should you wish only to be left alone, that too I understand.
Ser {player}, a word of caution from one who has changed banners before: the new hall rarely smells as sweet as promised.
Your departure from {my_faction} is noted, ser {player}. Let us see whether {faction} proves worthy of the sword you have given it.
I bear you no grudge, nor any warmth. Keep your word to {faction} and we shall have nothing to discuss.

global.text: Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Our hall is quieter for it, but I wish them fortune on the road ahead.
Pity to lose a sword as true as ser {player}'s. I still name them a fine companion, whatever banner they now carry.
Let it be known: the door of {my_faction} remains unbarred for ser {player}, should {faction} ever fail them.
Some will call {player} a turncloak. I call them a traveller who followed their heart, and I hold no quarrel with that.
The feasts will miss ser {player}'s laughter. May {faction} prove a worthy hearth, though none could replace our table.
Ser {player} has chosen a new road, and I bear them no ill will. Our cups remain full should they ever return.

whisper.text: I confess your leaving stings, ser {player}, yet I cannot hate a companion who fought beside me. Go with my blessing.
We bled together on the eastern marches, ser {player}. That memory outlasts any banner. I hope {faction} treats you well.
Should {faction} disappoint you, ser {player}, send word. My table will remember you, and the door will open.
Do not think I have forgotten our oaths sworn in the mead hall. You are still a friend, though a far-off one now.
The company will be the poorer without you, ser {player}. Keep your honour bright in {faction}'s service, friend.
Forgive my sulking, ser {player}. I am wounded, but a wound is not the same as a grudge, and I bear you none.

global.text: The smoke rising from {village} shall be remembered by every hearth in the realm. {player} will answer for it.
They put {village} to the torch while its men were abroad. A cowardly hand, and I shall not forget the name {player}.
Let all who trade with {player} know: such a fire does not burn out without a reckoning.
Ash where {village} once stood. My ancestors weep, and I have sworn their vengeance upon {player}.
Some find glory in burning hamlets. I find only a stain upon a name, and {player} wears it proudly.
{village} lies in ruin tonight, and the one who set the torches is {player}. Let no one call that a victory.
Bards will sing of {village}'s grief long after {player} has forgotten the taste of this smoke.
Do not mistake my patience for mercy. {player} has lit the fire, and I will be the one to snuff it.

whisper.text: You burned {village} while its people slept, ser {player}. Such deeds have a way of returning to the one who lit them.
Another night of your torches, another ruin. I am tired of counting your sins, ser {player}.
Meet me at the old ford and bring your courage, if any remains after {village}. I would have words with you.
I will not forgive the ashes of {village}, nor the children who ran from them. Know that, friend.
Your banner is a shame to every honest house, {player}. I hope you sleep soundly, for I certainly will not.
The people of {village} asked me to speak for them. I speak now: stay out of the lands I guard.
A fire set in cowardice is still a fire, and it leaves its mark on the one who kindled it, {player}.
Should our paths cross on the road, draw your blade, ser {player}. I will not turn my face from you again.

global.text: Word has reached the market that {village} was burned. I make no judgement yet, but I am watching, {player}.
Some say {player} acted from necessity, others from appetite. The ashes of {village} speak plainly enough.
The roads are less quiet since {village} burned. Travellers, mind your company, and mind the company of {player}.
I have no quarrel to declare with anyone today, though the smoke over {village} still troubles my thoughts.
A lord's word is worth more than his torches. Let {player} answer to the council of this realm, not to rumour.
{village} has been wounded and will mend. Its people are stubborn. I wonder whether {player} understands that.
Nothing about the burning of {village} sits well with me, though I have seen worse done by better folk.
Let it be recorded that I do not stand with those who burned {village}, nor will I speak for them yet.

whisper.text: I have heard of the fire at {village}, ser {player}. I would hear your account before I judge it.
We have never crossed blades, you and I. Let us keep it that way, and I will keep my own counsel about {village}.
Was the burning of {village} a matter of honour, or of coin? Tell me plainly, friend, and I shall listen.
I do not wish to be your enemy, ser {player}, but I will not be your ally while {village} lies in ash.
Some debts are paid in silver and some in apology. The people of {village} are owed the second, ser {player}.
Keep your distance from my holdings, ser {player}. What passes between us after {village} is for time to decide.
The fire at {village} has made me careful, and carefulness is a habit I am reluctant to abandon for anyone.
If you came to my door seeking a kindly word, you will find none today. Only questions about {village}.

global.text: Ser {player} has been speaking of renown in every tavern. Let them wear their fame while it lasts, for the wind turns in the spring.
I have heard the name {player} sung in three halls this week. A song is cheap, ser, and so is the breath that sings it.
Ser {player} rides on borrowed glory. When the tide finds them, I shall be standing on the shore to watch them drown.
Such a fuss over a single skirmish. Mark me, the name of {player} will be forgotten before the harvest moon.
Gods preserve us from ambition in a fresh-made champion. {player} has yet to bleed for anything that truly matters.
Ser {player}, I grant you a fine reputation. I shall ask at the next council whether it was earned or merely shouted.
Ser {player} is much talked of now. I shall withhold judgement until I see whether the talk has any substance behind it.
So the road has made a new name. I have walked a long way and seen many names rise, so I wait and watch, traveller.
Renown is a curious coin, friend. Some spend it well, others melt it down in drink. Which sort is {player}?
I note that {player} is growing famous. Fame is pleasant company, though it keeps poor counsel at the hearth.
Whatever the chroniclers write of {player}, the ledger of deeds will close only when the last banner has fallen.
Ser {player}, your name travels faster than your horse. Be sure your feet keep pace with the tale.
Ser {player} has earned every word of praise. The hall of my house keeps a seat warm for them whenever they wish it.
Rejoice, friends! Ser {player} rises in renown, and the ancestors look kindly upon this realm for it.
I swore an oath to stand beside the worthy, and {player} has proven worthy twice over. Let the bards sing it loud.
A toast to {player}, whose name now carries farther than any herald could shout it. May the road remain generous.
Ser {player}, I am glad to call you friend before all the realm. Keep your honour bright and your blade steady.
The chronicles will record {player} as one who rose by courage, not by boasting. I am proud to have witnessed it.
{fief} was taken by treachery, not by valour. Let every hall in the realm remember who now wears its stolen banner.
So {player} now sits in {fief}. Enjoy the draughts, ser. Stone walls keep out thieves far better than they keep out memory.
I expected little from {player}, yet even I did not expect a wall to be bought so cheaply.
Mark it well: {fief} fell to a cunning raid, not a fair siege. Such victories sour quickly in the mouth.
The gates of {fief} now open for a usurper. I will have them back, and my ancestors will witness it.
Ser {player} may hold {fief} tonight. Let them savour it, for the stones remember whose hands raised them.

whisper.text: You have my stones now, ser {player}. Keep them warm, for I have a long memory and a longer patience.
Enjoy {fief} while its walls still stand. I will be counting the nights you spend behind them.
A castle taken in the dark is still a castle taken. Do not mistake my silence for surrender.
Mind the wine in the cellars of {fief}, ser {player}. It was poured by a steward with a grudge.
Your bannermen will tire of guarding a fortress that does not love them. I will wait for that day.
You have taken {fief} and a debt along with it, ser {player}. Debts in this realm are always collected.

global.text: {fief} has changed hands again. I take no side in the matter, but I note who is now counting the coin.
The walls of {fief} are in new hands. Good fortune to {player}, though I suspect the next siege is not far off.
Some say {player} took {fief} by cunning, others by coin. I say only that the reckoning is not yet written.
Word travels slowly on these roads, yet it reached me that {player} now holds {fief}. I shall reserve judgment.
A quiet morning's work at {fief}, if the rumours are true. Let the chroniclers decide the rest.
{fief} has a new keeper of its gates. I wish {player} the patience to hold what they have won.

whisper.text: I have no quarrel with you over {fief}, ser {player}. Keep it well, and we shall speak civilly when next we meet.
The fall of {fief} was clever work. I would be glad to hear how you came by the postern, should you care to share.
I shall not pretend the loss stings less for being fairly won. Hold {fief} well, friend.
Do not expect me to thank you for {fief}, ser {player}, nor to curse you for it. The road is long and so is memory.
If you need a second opinion on the walls of {fief}, send word. I know those stones better than most.
No blood has been spilt between us yet, ser {player}. Let us keep it so while the realm is watching.

global.text: Another victory for ser {player}? Lucky streaks end, friend, and I shall be waiting when this one does.
They call ser {player} unbeaten. Strange, for I have not yet met a foe who truly tried.
Ser {player} wins so often that the bards have run out of verses. Pity the bards.
A dozen fields won and the crowd cheers as if the war were over. It is not over, good people.
Let the ballads sing of ser {player} all they like. Ballads have never yet held a castle.
Ser {player}'s banner rises again. Enjoy the view from the top, for the fall is always steeper.
Honour, they say, follows ser {player}. Then honour has poor taste in company.
Every battle won by ser {player} is one more reason for the rest of us to grow sharper blades.

whisper.text: You have won a great many fields of late, ser {player}. Enjoy them while the ground still holds you.
Do not mistake a run of luck for a reckoning, ser {player}. I keep a long ledger and your name is on it.
Your victories grow loud, and loud men attract sharper blades than mine. Consider yourself warned.
I have counted your wins, ser {player}. Each one is a debt, and I am a patient creditor.
Sleep lightly, ser {player}. A winning streak makes a rival either fearful or foolish, and I am neither.
Your fortune is admired by many and envied by more. I count myself among the second group.
When your luck turns, ser {player}, I shall be there to witness it with a cup in hand.
Let us speak plainly. Your banners are everywhere and your enemies are gathering. Choose your road with care.

global.text: Ser {player} has won several fields in succession. I shall wait to see whether the streak holds past the harvest.
A remarkable run of victories. Remarkable things have a way of ending, and then we learn what they were made of.
The tally of ser {player}'s battles grows long. I neither cheer nor sneer, for the roads will tell the tale.
Many now speak of ser {player}'s triumphs. I have heard those tales before, and I will reserve my judgement.
Ser {player} keeps winning. It is good for the markets, at least, as the mercenaries are well paid.
Victories in a row are pleasant to watch from a distance. Less pleasant when they are watched from a ditch.
Honour to ser {player} for the recent fields. Let the next season show whether fortune or skill carried them.
The banners of ser {player} have been seen on many roads this season. Travellers speak of little else.

whisper.text: Your recent victories are the talk of the realm, ser {player}. I wonder whether you enjoy the attention.
Ser {player}, you have been winning steadily. Would you care to share the secret, or is it simply a strong arm?
I have no quarrel with you, ser {player}, though I hear your name often. Fortune favours some more than others.
A word of caution, friend. Streaks like yours draw eyes, and not all of them are friendly.
Your sword has been busy of late, ser {player}. I hope it is not thirsting for more than it needs.
Ser {player}, I have read the reports of your wins. Let us speak when your road and mine cross.
Many have praised your battles, ser {player}. I prefer to see the next one before I offer praise.
Do you keep count of your victories, ser {player}? I find I have lost track, and I have been watching closely.

global.text: Ser {player} has been winning in every field lately. Let the next toast be raised to them and their steady hand.
The ancestors must be smiling on ser {player}. I have never seen such a run of honest victories.
Three cheers for ser {player}! Each battle won is a story worth telling around the hearth.
Ser {player} fights as though the ground itself owes them a debt. Long may that fortune last.
The bards will need a longer song for ser {player}. I gladly lend my voice to the chorus.
Friends, mark the name of ser {player}. We shall speak of these fields for many winters yet.
Ser {player} has brought honour to our banners this season. I am proud to share a cause with them.
Another win for ser {player}. Good fortune to them, and may their next challenger be a worthy one.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, your recent victories have stirred my heart. Should you ever need a shield beside you, call on me.
Ser {player}, I am glad to see such fine fortune. Let us drink together when the dust has settled.
Your string of wins puts my own deeds to shame, ser {player}. I shall toast you, though I might grumble first.
Well fought, ser {player}. Every field you win is one fewer my friends must risk their necks upon.
Ser {player}, I have followed your battles with great interest. Tell me, what is your next road?
Come, ser {player}, you have earned a rest. Your name is spoken with respect in every hall I visit.
My loyalty to you has never wavered, ser {player}, and your recent triumphs have only strengthened it.
A fine season, ser {player}. Should the bards fall silent, I will gladly carry the tune for you.

global.text: Ser {player} let me walk free rather than name a price. A sly mercy, and I will not thank it aloud.
They released me without a ransom. Some call that honour; I call it a debt I never asked to owe.
Ser {player} forwent my ransom today. Let the hall note the gift. I shall repay it with steel, not thanks.
Ransom refused, prisoner loosed. Ser {player} has made a fool of every purse in this land.
Ser {player} could have bled my treasury dry. Instead they opened the gate. I trust that gate less than a coin.
A free man again, and no thanks to {player}'s purse. I will remember who humbled my pride this week.
Ser {player} chose mercy over gold. Bold, or foolish. Time will tell which the ancestors favour.
They loosed me with no ransom paid. The next meeting between us will settle the account, not the coin.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you loosed me without ransom. Do not mistake my silence for gratitude. We have an account open.
I owe you nothing, ser {player}. Your mercy was a poor bargain and I will not forget the cost to my pride.
Freed without ransom by your hand. I would sooner have rotted in the cell than owe you a single thing.
Ser {player}, a release is not a friendship. Be wary when next our roads cross, for I walk them with a grudge.
You gave me back my freedom and took my dignity with it. That is a trade I did not agree to, ser {player}.
I did not ask for your pity. Next time, name a ransom and keep your mercy in your purse.
Mercy from a rival is a hook in disguise, ser {player}. I have seen it before and I see it now.
Enjoy the victory of a cheap release, ser {player}. The debt you refused to collect will be paid another way.

global.text: Ser {player} has loosed a prisoner without a ransom. An odd custom for these roads, and I shall watch to see where it leads.
Freedom given freely is rare coin in these parts. Whether it was wisdom or whim, only time will tell.
I hear a captive was released by {player} with no price set. Curious. Mercy has a way of returning like a debt.
A release without ransom makes a fine tale for the tavern. I will judge its ending when it is written.
No gold changed hands, only a gate opened. Weighing that, I am uncertain what sort of noble walks these roads.
The prisoner was loosed by {player} for nothing. The ancestors may approve. I am still deciding my own view.
Some will call that generosity, others a poor accounting. I leave the matter to the hall's gossip, for now.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you released me without a ransom. I am grateful, but I am not yet sure what you expect in return.
Your mercy was unexpected. I shall keep my blade sheathed and my counsel closed until I understand your aim, ser {player}.
You chose to free me rather than sell me back. I do not know yet whether that makes you a friend or a puzzle.
Ser {player}, I thank you for the open gate. Let us speak again when the roads have shown us what we are to one another.
A release, not a ransom. Few would have done it. I will remember the choice, though not yet the reason behind it.
I owe you no coin now, ser {player}. Whether I owe you more than that, I have not decided. Ask me again later.
Walk your road and I will walk mine. Your mercy has given us both an odd beginning, ser {player}.
Ser {player}, I have heard the release was not for gold. I wonder what coin you did seek instead.

global.text: Ser {player} freed me without ransom. Such honour is rare; I name them generous before all.
The gate opened and no ransom was named. Praise the ancestors for placing such a noble heart on these roads.
Ser {player} loosed a captive for nothing but the right thing. Let every banner in the land know of this deed.
Freed by {player}, not bought back. I shall owe this mercy my whole life and count the debt a joy.
Ser {player} spared me the price of my own chains. I swear on my house's name that I will repay this kindness.
A fine act, unbought and unbargained. Ser {player} has shown the realm what chivalry still looks like.
Let it be sung that {player} opened a prison gate without a demand for gold. Such generosity is a rare bloom.
I walked free today because of {player}'s mercy alone. My sword and my name are yours, friend, whenever you call.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, you released me when a ransom would have been easier. I will not forget this, nor the honour behind it.
My freedom was a gift, not a bargain. I thank you, ser {player}, and I shall hold my oath to you as dear as my life.
You could have named a price and did not. Your mercy has bound me closer than any contract could, ser {player}.
Ser {player}, the gate you opened is one I will carry in my heart. Call on me when a banner needs holding.
I am free because you chose mercy over gold. My ancestors would approve, and so do I, friend.
There are few nobles who would release a stranger without asking coin. You are one, ser {player}. I salute you.
Ser {player}, I count your mercy as the finest thing that befell me this year. Let me repay you in deed.
Thank you, ser {player}, for opening the gate without a ransom. Name the day and I shall stand beside you.

global.text: Let the heralds carry word across every hall: {enemy_faction} has forced our hand, and {my_faction} will answer in steel.
I weep for {enemy_faction}, for they have chosen a quarrel with a house that does not forget a slight.
Ser, the bells of {my_faction} ring for war tonight, and every soul who bears our colours is sworn to the field.
Our grandsires would laugh to see {enemy_faction} march against us. Let them come and count the cost.
Bread and blades must be counted now. {my_faction} wishes no bloodshed, yet shows no mercy to oath breakers.
Mark this day, travellers: the quarrel with {enemy_faction} is no longer a rumour, and the ledgers of honour lie open.
Ha! {enemy_faction} wishes for war, and I confess I had hoped to be bored this summer. Pray they bring better wine.
{enemy_faction} has taken our fishing rights at the mill pond. A petty theft, yet a theft against honour all the same.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, I do not trust easily, yet {enemy_faction} threatens us both. Shall we speak terms?
We have little cause to love one another, ser {player}, but the banners of {enemy_faction} grow bold. Consider an alliance.
I keep my own counsel, traveller, but a common foe makes strange bedfellows. Would you ride with me against {enemy_faction}?
My ancestors would scorn me for trusting a stranger, ser {player}, yet I trust {enemy_faction} less. Name your terms.
Let us not pretend to be friends. Let us be sensible, and strike at {enemy_faction} together before they strike us.
Weary of this feud, ser {player}. {enemy_faction} gains ground while we squabble. A truce against them may serve us both.
I offer no sworn bond yet, only a question: will you stand against {enemy_faction} at my side, for a season?
The road ahead is long and {enemy_faction} waits upon it. I would rather walk it with a wary companion than alone.
Ser {player}, you have been a true companion to me, and now {enemy_faction} seeks our ruin. Let us bind our swords together.
My friend, I would sooner share my bread with you than with {enemy_faction}. Shall we swear an alliance against them?
Our names are already woven together in my heart, traveller. Let that bond become a shield against {enemy_faction}.
Ser {player}, I have never regretted standing beside you. Stand beside me once more against {enemy_faction}, I beg you.
Should {enemy_faction} march upon your holdings, you will find my banner already raised beside yours. Swear with me.
Such loyalty as yours deserves a worthy cause, ser {player}. {enemy_faction} is that cause, and I would fight it with you.
A fine evening for a pact, friend. Let us swear before the sun sets that {enemy_faction} shall find us united.
Ser {player}, speak the word and I will call my knights to arms. Together we shall break {enemy_faction}'s pride.
Ser {player}, I will not dress this up. {fief} is failing and I need hands that are not my own. Will you lend yours?
I owe you no favour, ser {player}, yet {fief} is besieged and I am desperate. Name your price and I will hear it.
They say your blade is for hire. Then hire it to {fief}, ser {player}, before {enemy_faction} takes the walls by dawn.
Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} has taken two villages from me and I have no men to answer. Could you spare any?
I do not ask out of affection, ser {player}. I ask because {fief} will fall without aid, and a fallen fief helps no one.
Weary as I am, I write to you. {fief} bleeds, {enemy_faction} grows bolder, and I have run out of pride to spend.
Should you remain idle while {fief} burns, ser {player}, history will remember your silence longer than my pleas.
Consider it a bargain, ser {player}. Ride to {fief} and drive off {enemy_faction}, and my gratitude will be recorded in full.
My dear friend {player}, {fief} is in peril and there is no one whose sword I trust more than yours. Come, I beg you.
Ser {player}, you have stood beside me before. Now {fief} needs that loyalty once more, and I dare not ask another.
Our oath of friendship binds us, ser {player}. {enemy_faction} presses at {fief}'s gates and I cannot hold them alone.
Friend {player}, forgive the hour. {fief} is under siege and my heart told me to write to you before anyone else.
Recall the feast we shared, ser {player}. Those same walls now shelter our kin, and {enemy_faction} means to breach them.
Friend {player}, I hate to trouble you, but {fief} totters and {enemy_faction} smells blood. I need you there.
The ancestors who raised {fief} will not forgive me if it falls, ser {player}. Ride with me and let us save it together.
Whatever we have spoken of before, ser {player}, I count you among those I would trust with my last wall. Will you answer?
Ser {player}, I have grown weary of hearing your name praised. Meet me at the old ford at dawn and prove it.
You fled from me like a hound from a thrown stone, ser {player}. Stand on the hill above {village} and face me.
Your banner still hangs crooked in the hall at {town}, ser {player}. Meet me in the field and I will set it straight.
A grudge left to rot grows teeth, ser {player}. I am done waiting. Meet me at the crossroads beyond {village} and end it.
Sleep poorly tonight, ser {player}, for I have sworn to settle our quarrel in single combat. Name the place and the hour.
Ser {player}, I hear you keep a squire to carry your shield. Come and fight me yourself, unless your squire is the braver of you.
My ancestors would weep to see your insults go unanswered, ser {player}. Meet me at dusk beside the old standing stones.
Ser {player}. Dawn, the mill road outside {town}. Come alone, or do not come at all.
Ser {player}, I bear you no grudge, yet fate keeps us in each other's way. Shall we test our blades at {village}?
I have watched your footwork in the square at {town}, ser {player}. I would see whether it holds against a true challenger.
Take no offence, ser {player}, but I trust no stranger's smile. Meet me in open ground and show me your honour.
I have no appetite for feuds, ser {player}, yet one honest duel might spare us a year of whispers. Dawn at {village}?
A blade crossed in fair challenge teaches more than a hundred polite greetings, friend. Will you cross steel with me at {town}?
Friend, the road between us grows narrower each season. Let us widen it with a bout of arms by the well at {village}.
Our houses dispute a boundary near {village}. I would sooner argue it with swords than with ink, ser {player}.
Ser {player}, I invite you to single combat at the gate of {town} when the bells ring noon. Accept or decline, as honour allows.
Your name is spoken often in taverns, ser {player}, and never once with admiration. Bold of you to keep walking so proudly.
Do not mistake my silence for mercy, traveller. I have simply not yet decided how much of your pride I wish to take.
I wonder whether your ancestors knew how loudly their line would be embarrassed, ser {player}. I suspect they would weep.
A hound that barks at every shadow soon forgets which shadow bites. Consider that before you strut past my gate again, friend.
Some are remembered for their deeds. You, ser {player}, will be remembered for the coins you begged.
Weary as I am of hearing {player} boast, I almost pity the poor soul who must endure it daily.
A ballad is being written about your last defeat, ser {player}. The chorus is one long, mournful sigh. I have heard it myself.
{rival} sends regards and a warning: they wagered a fine horse you will flee before the next moon. I took that bet.
